Beat 15 egg yolks, half a kilogram (one pound) of beaten sugar, and a piece of vanilla or lemon zest for 1/4 hour
Fold in stiff egg white snow from 15 egg whites
Gradually add the dried potato flour, about one tablespoon at a time (half a kilogram or one pound total)

title: Zmrzlina (Ice Cream)
description: Prepared with ice and salt.
steps: Line the container in which ice cream is to be made in a smaller container with ice broken into pieces and salted to produce greater cold
Chill the ice cream container for at least ten minutes by rapidly rotating it until completely cooled
Clean it, fill with ice cream mixture and rotate and whip it rapidly until it begins to cool and harden
Open the lid which must be firmly attached, scrape the sides of the container and in the sealed container the ice cream is again whipped and mixed much more rapidly than before
After a while stop again, scrape everything and repeat several times until the ice cream is completely ready
Place the ice cream in decorative containers and molds
Remove ice cream from molds by placing it in warm water, warming it and turning the ice cream out onto a plate
Paint the outside of the ice cream with fruit juice from the fruit which the mold should resemble, so that it also has that taste

title: Úhoř na modro (Blued Eel)
description: Prepared with eel, celery, and carrot.
steps: Fix the eel to the table with a fork
Make an incision around the head just below the skin and pull off the skin using a cloth, being careful not to break the gall bladder which is located under the skin near the head
Clean and cut the eel into pieces
Place celery, parsley, carrot and onion (all sliced) in a pot along with a bay leaf, a piece of sage, several peppercorns and allspice
Salt and add enough vinegar and let simmer for half an hour
Add the cut eel pieces to this sauce, add a glass of wine and enough more vinegar so the eel is completely covered
Continue simmering gently for another quarter hour
Arrange the eel on a dish and strain the sauce through a fine sieve into a serving dish

For the hollandaise-style sauce: place a spoonful of white flour in a bowl, add a little cold water and mix well, add six egg yolks, add four spoonfuls of fresh butter and mix well, add twelve white peppercorns and a little nutmeg
Pour in a pint of the water in which the eel was cooked
Place over heat and stir constantly until it is about to boil, but do not let it boil
Squeeze in the juice of half a lemon and strain through a fine sieve into a serving bowl

description: Prepared with oysters, juice, and beef or fish broth.

Make a light roux from a spoonful of butter and a spoonful of flour in a pan

Salt, pepper and let simmer for about ten minutes
Beat two egg yolks or a whole egg with a spoonful of butter and lemon juice
Mix this into the sauce, strain it through a sieve, and keeping it constantly stirred over the fire, let it heat through—but it must not boil

title: Šampaňské Víno z Ovoce (Sparkling Fruit Wine)
description: Prepared with pears.
steps: Sparkling wine is best made from juicy, ripe pears.
Grate and press the pears; pour the juice into a barrel or bottles depending on the quantity, tie the opening with cloth only, and let everything rest peacefully.
Within two to three days the juice begins to ferment, foam develops and pushes out of the opening.
When the foam subsides, fill the bottles and barrel with fermented fruit juice, seal the opening tightly, and place the containers in a cool cellar for several weeks (five to six).
After this time, siphon the clarified juice through a tap into strong bottles, seal them tightly, bind with wire and seal with wax or pitch.
This method produces very tasty sparkling wine.
If three parts pear juice and one part raspberry juice are taken, with the same treatment a very good, lovely wine is obtained.
If the wine is allowed to ferment completely and rest in the cellar for a full year so that it loses carbonation, a very good drinkable wine is obtained.

title: Žitný Chléb (Rye Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with rye or dough or water, yeast or liquid, and rye flour.

ingredients.name: rye dough saved from previous baking, or two cups lukewarm water
dried yeast or compressed yeast or one cup liquid yeast

steps: For the rye bread starter, it is best to keep a piece of dough from one baking to the next, about two tablespoons
The day before baking, pour about two cups of lukewarm water over the dough to soften it
In the evening, mix it well, add flour to make a thin starter like for pancakes and let it rise in a warm place overnight

If you do not have dough from the previous baking, take two cups of lukewarm water in the evening before baking, in which you have soaked one square of dry yeast or a piece of compressed yeast, or pour in one cup of liquid yeast
Add enough rye flour so that the dough is slightly thicker than for pancakes, mix it well into a smooth starter
If desired, add fennel or caraway seeds or both and let it rise well in a warm place until morning

In the morning, add one quart of lukewarm water to the starter, in which you have mixed one quarter teaspoon of baking soda, season with salt, add as much flour as needed and work the dough thoroughly with a wooden spoon so that it does not stick to the bowl or hands
Dust again with flour, cover with a warm cloth and let it rise again for about one and one-half hours
Then roll out the dough on a floured board, shape into a loaf, place on a sheet, let it rise again, place it in a well-heated oven and bake for at least two hours
For one loaf, one usually counts one quart of water and four pounds of flour; however, each cook must learn the exact amount of flour from her own experience

description: Prepared with rice and water.

Throw the washed rice into a good sized kettle in which a considerable quantity of water is boiling rapidly
